findings.evidence: project-settings-archive-link has href="#project-archived" (archiving commits immediately); the "archive-confirm" section (which has its own labeled Cancel and Archive controls and copy naming the consequence and restore path) has no element anywhere in the artifact linking to it with href="#archive-confirm", so it is unreachable from the control that actually performs the action.
findings.fix: Point project-settings-archive-link at #archive-confirm instead of #project-archived, and leave archive-confirm's own Archive control (which already targets #project-archived) as the one that commits, so the confirmation the artifact already wrote is the one the user's path actually reaches.
findings.violation: NNG-H5-CONFIRM requires a costly action's own path to reach a confirmation naming the object and consequence before it commits. The artifact defines exactly such a confirmation (archive-confirm), but the control the user has to invoke to archive bypasses it entirely and goes straight to the archived result. That control's path reaches neither a confirmation nor an undo, and archiving removes the project from the active list for everyone on the team on a single click.

findings.evidence: project-settings-save-btn and invite-member-save-btn are type=submit on forms with no action attribute and no stated outcome; notification-settings-save-btn (labeled "Submit") is the same; project-settings-duplicate-btn (type=button, aria-label "Duplicate project") has no href or target at all.
findings.fix: Specify a visible save confirmation (toast, inline message, or changed control state) for each save/submit action, and specify where the duplicate appears (e.g., a new entry in the workspace-overview project list) for Duplicate project.

instances.evidence: type=submit, form has no action attribute, no confirmation named
type=submit, form has no action attribute, no confirmation named
type=submit, labeled "Submit", form has no action attribute, no confirmation named
type=button, aria-label "Duplicate project", no href or target, no outcome named anywhere

findings.violation: NNG-H1 requires that every state-changing action the artifact describes name what the user sees while it runs and once it finishes. None of the three save/submit forms in this artifact specify a save confirmation, and the duplicate-project action specifies no outcome whatsoever, not even where a duplicated project would appear.

findings.fix: Pick one label for this commit action, for example "Save", and use it everywhere the action appears.
findings.violation: This artifact uses 2 different labels for what reads as the same commit action: "Save", "Submit". A user cannot tell from the label alone whether these controls perform the same action or different ones.

findings.evidence: invite-member-continue-link is a plain link to #invite-sent, not conditioned on the invite-member-email-input value or on invite-member-save-btn having been used; invite-sent's own copy reads "An invite was sent to the address entered above."
findings.fix: Gate invite-member-continue-link on a validated, saved email address (disable it until the input holds a valid value, or merge Save and Continue into one control), so invite-sent cannot be reached without an address behind it.
findings.violation: Nothing in the artifact constrains the order so that Continue can only be reached after a valid email has been entered and saved. A user can click Continue with the email field empty or unsaved and still land on a screen that states an invite was sent to an address, which is exactly the out-of-order completion NNG-H5-PREVENT asks to be designed out rather than surfaced after the fact.

findings.evidence: "The last import finished with 3 rows skipped: each referenced a project that does not exist in this workspace. Rows 63, 71, and 82 were skipped; every other row was imported." is followed only by import-status-exit-link, "Back to your projects".
findings.fix: Add a control on the import-status screen that acts on the specific failure, such as a link to re-upload the three skipped rows or to create the missing referenced projects, rather than only a path back to the overview.
findings.violation: The message identifies the specific rows and cause (satisfying NNG-H9-IDENTIFY), but NNG-H9-RECOVER requires a next step reachable from the error state itself. The only control on this screen returns to the general workspace overview; there is no retry, no re-import of the skipped rows, and no link to create or fix the missing referenced projects.
